heard: Saturn has an icy moon shaped like a sponge. When NASA's Cassini spacecraft arrived in 2005, its craters made no sense. Normal impacts blasted debris everywhere, but Hyperion had almost none. The answer is that 40% of Hyperion is empty space. Because it's porous water ice, meteors don't blast rock outward. They punch directly inward, compressing the ice like foam. Gravitational tugs from giant Titan also keep Hyperion tumbling chaotically. Its spin wobbles through space in completely unpredictable directions. That wild tumble belongs to Saturn's strangest frozen world.
